title: Telemetry: export Dedicated pool queue depth + utilization metrics for staged rollout gates
author: Caleb Johnson
body:
Context: Dedicated staged rollouts need gate inputs that correlate strongly with saturation and user-visible queuing. Today we have some node-level GPU metrics, but we don't export pool-scoped queue depth and we don't have a consistent utilization signal that the gate evaluator can query safely with low cardinality.

This PR adds first-class metrics for Dedicated reserved pools and wires them through the telemetry pipeline so the gate evaluator (PR #28490) and SRE dashboards (observability-pack PR #913) can depend on them.

What changed: (1) Export pool-scoped queue depth and request concurrency from the pool scheduler (data plane) with explicit cardinality constraints. (2) Export pool-scoped GPU utilization aggregated at the pool level (avg + p95) derived from per-GPU samples but emitted with pool_id only. (3) Add a small set of standard labels expected by gate queries: tenant_id, pool_id, region, model_family (optional; off by default for high-volume pools). (4) Add links to the rollout gate dashboards in code comments next to the metric definitions so oncall can jump directly from source -> graph.

New metrics (Prometheus): redwood_dedicated_pool_queue_depth{tenant_id,pool_id,region} (gauge) => current pending requests in pool queue; redwood_dedicated_pool_inflight_requests{tenant_id,pool_id,region} (gauge) => currently executing requests in the pool; redwood_dedicated_pool_gpu_utilization_avg{tenant_id,pool_id,region} (gauge) => pool-level avg utilization (0-1); redwood_dedicated_pool_gpu_utilization_p95{tenant_id,pool_id,region} (gauge) => pool-level p95 utilization (0-1); redwood_dedicated_pool_metrics_staleness_seconds{tenant_id,pool_id,region} (gauge) => time since last successful scrape/emit; used by the evaluator missing-metrics hold behavior.

Cardinality / perf notes: pool_id is bounded by Dedicated pools; tenant_id is bounded by Dedicated tenants. We do not include route_id or model_version in these signals. model_family label is behind a config flag (defaults false) and is only emitted for allowlisted pools where it helps debugging without exploding series count.

Dashboards: This PR doesn’t add dashboards directly, but it includes direct links (Grafana) in comments for the relevant panels: "Dedicated Rollouts / Gate Signals" and "Dedicated Rollouts / Evaluator Health". The dashboards themselves land in observability-pack PR #913.

Testing: unit tests for metric emission + label validation; integration test in staging verifying series existence and staleness behavior; manual validation by replaying a synthetic queue surge on a dev reserved pool and confirming queue_depth follows.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag telemetry.dedicated_pool_gate_metrics_enabled (default off in prod). We’ll enable for dogfood Dedicated pools first, then flip on for beta allowlist tenants.

Follow-ups: tighten aggregation behavior for very large pools (sampling) and unify naming with the final gate query templates once ADR-027 queries are finalized.
commits: telemetry(dedicated): export pool queue depth + inflight metrics from scheduler
telemetry(dedicated): add pool-scoped GPU utilization aggregation (avg/p95)
telemetry: enforce label allowlist + add staleness gauge for gate safety
docs: add Grafana links in metric definition comments
tests: add emission + cardinality guard tests
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we confirm none of these metrics include model_version/route_id? We had issues before where a “helpful” label exploded series count.

Caleb Johnson (author): Yep—explicitly blocked. label_policy.go now rejects route_id/model_version for these metric names. Added a test that fails if those labels appear. model_family is behind a config flag and defaults off.
Sean Gallagher (review): Gate evaluator needs a way to detect missing/late metrics. Does staleness_seconds reflect scrape gaps or emission gaps?

Caleb Johnson (author): Emission gap. It’s updated on successful emit from the scheduler; if the dataplane stops emitting (or exporter rejects), it grows. This is the signal the evaluator can use to "pause rather than proceed".
Keiko Yamamoto (review): Queue depth semantics: is this pre-admission (before rate limiting) or post-admission (work actually waiting for GPUs)? Gates should key off the latter.
Caleb Johnson (author): Post-admission. It’s the scheduler’s internal pending queue for workers. I updated the metric docstring to call that out explicitly.
Logan Wright (review): Requesting changes: utilization aggregation should use the same sampling interval across pools, and label_policy should be enforced at registration time too (not just emit).
Caleb Johnson (author): Addressed: added a fixed 10s sampling window in the aggregator + enforced label policy at metric registration (registry_dedicated.go). Reran CI.
Mina Haddad (review): This looks good. One nit: can we add the dashboard link for the “Pool Saturation” panel as well? That’s the one routing/oncall will look at first.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added a second link in the metric comment block to the Pool Saturation panel (same folder).
Logan Wright (review): Approved. Thanks for taking the time on cardinality guardrails—this will save us later.
Sean Gallagher (review): Approved. Please ensure the prod flag stays off until dogfood load test is complete (link in ENG-5132).
Caleb Johnson (author): Ack—left default false; enablement will be via per-env override only.
release_notes: Added Dedicated pool queue depth, inflight requests, and pool-scoped GPU utilization metrics (behind feature flag) for staged rollout gate evaluation.
